text: The guy next to you on the train lets out a monster sneeze.
note: Fires automatically. 'Gesundheit' is the casual alt.

text: Packed bus. Someone's standing right in your path, back turned.
note: The natural line for slipping by. 'Scuse me' also works.

text: At the coffee counter you back straight into someone. Their latte wobbles.
note: Instant apology. The 'oh gosh' makes it real, not stiff.

text: The waiter slides your plate in front of you: 'Enjoy.'
note: Natives react to the food, not just say 'thank you'.

text: Your arms are full and a stranger holds the door open with their foot.
sample: Oh, you're the best — thank you!
note: Warm, natural thanks for a small kindness.

text: Your scarf slips off. A stranger scoops it up and holds it out.
note: Warmth in the 'oh' — sounds genuine, not flat.

text: Glasses go up around the table, everyone looking at you.
note: Universal toast. Say it, don't just clink.

text: The door clicks shut behind you — and your keys are on the other side.
sample: Oh, you have got to be kidding me.
chunk: you have got to be kidding me
note: Classic frustration reflex. Milder: 'Ah, not again!'

text: A neighbor holds out a plate: 'Fresh from the oven — take one.'
sample: Oh, don't mind if I do — thanks!
note: Warm, playful 'yes' to an offer — like you're being talked into it.

text: 'Come on, have some more,' they say, tilting the dish at you. You're full.
sample: I'm good, honestly — thank you though.
note: The soft, friendly decline. Never a flat 'no'.

text: You and a stranger arrive at the narrow doorway at the exact same moment.
note: Polite reflex to wave someone through first.

text: The cashier says something but the coffee machine drowns it out.
note: Softer than 'what?'. 'Sorry, come again?' works too.

text: Your phone lights up — it's your best friend: 'I GOT THE JOB!!'
note: 'No way' carries the excitement. Land it, then 'congrats'.

text: Your friend's voice cracks: 'We had to put the dog down last night.'
note: The pause and 'oh no' do the emotional work here.

text: You spot an old friend across the street — you haven't seen them in years.
note: The reunion reflex. Fires the second you recognize them.

text: After hauling boxes all day, your friend flops down: 'You're the best, seriously.'
note: Warmer than 'you're welcome'. Waves off the thanks.

text: Someone looks you up and down: 'That jacket looks great on you.'
sample: Oh, thank you — that's so kind!
note: Take the compliment. Don't brush it off with 'no, no'.

text: A new face at the party sticks out a hand: 'Hi, I'm Sam.'
note: Echoing their name back sounds warm and switched-on.

text: The cake comes out, candles blazing, everyone turns to your friend.
note: Add 'hope it's a good one!' for the natural extra beat.

text: Your friend, pale outside the interview room: 'God, I'm so nervous.'
sample: Hey, you've got this. Good luck!
note: Reassurance reflex. Confident and warm, not preachy.

text: They rush in, breathless: 'I'm so sorry I'm late!'
sample: No worries at all — take your time.
note: Instantly defuses their panic. Very common reflex.

text: She stands and grabs her bag: 'Anyway, I should get going.'
sample: Aw, already? It was so good seeing you!
chunk: it was so good seeing you
note: The warm goodbye. 'Aw, already?' softens the parting.

text: Your friend leans in, lowering their voice: 'Okay, don't tell anyone, but—'
note: Pulls the story out of them. 'You're kidding!' is a cousin.

text: You slip into the meeting five minutes late; heads turn toward you.
sample: Sorry I'm late — please, carry on.
note: Apologize once, hand the floor back. Don't over-explain.

text: Your manager freezes on the call, then: '...so can you take that?' You caught none of it.
sample: Sorry, you cut out — could you say that again?
note: The exact phrase for bad audio. Everyone uses it.

text: Your boss drops a folder on your desk: 'Need this by five.'
note: Confident. Signals you're starting right now.

text: The room goes quiet — everyone's waiting for your answer.
sample: Good question — let me think for a sec.
chunk: let me think for a sec
note: Buys a beat and sounds thoughtful, not stuck.

text: A colleague drifts past your desk: 'Hey, how's it going?'
You hit send — then spot the typo sitting right in the subject line.
sample: Ugh — my bad, fixing it now.
note: Quick, casual ownership. Fine in most teams.

text: Everyone's settled, coffees down, screens up, all looking at you to kick off.
note: 'Alright' is the natural signal the meeting's kicking off.

text: It's midnight and your teammate is still there, squashing your bug with you.
note: Grateful reflex for someone going above and beyond.

text: A colleague slides the half-finished task over: 'It's all yours now.'
sample: Great — I'll take it from here.

text: 'Thanks so much for covering my shift,' your coworker says.
sample: No problem at all — happy to help.
note: Professional and warm. 'Anytime' is the casual version.

text: Your friend says the exact thing you were about to say.
note: Strong agreement. 'Couldn't agree more' is the big version.

text: Someone pitches a plan you quietly don't buy: 'It'll be fine, trust me.'
sample: Hmm... I'm not so sure about that.
chunk: I'm not so sure about that
note: Soft disagreement that keeps things friendly.

text: Your friend spins their laptop around to show off what they made.
note: Quick, natural appreciation — the tone carries it.

text: 'Bad news,' they sigh, 'the trip's off.'
note: The go-to sympathy line for a letdown.

text: Waiter, menus in hand: 'Table by the window, or the bar?' You genuinely don't mind.
note: Easygoing reflex. 'I don't mind either way' is the twin.

text: A car cuts in front of you — you stamp the brakes just in time.
note: Pure relief reflex after a near miss.

text: You stop mid-sentence — the meeting you promised to join was an hour ago.
note: 'It totally slipped my mind' is the slightly softer version.

text: The elevator doors are sliding shut and someone sprints toward them.
note: Reflex as you jab the button to save them.

text: The waiter passes and catches your eye: 'How's everything tasting?'
A store clerk drifts over while you browse: 'Finding everything okay?'
note: Polite way to say you don't need help yet.

text: An unknown number lights up your phone. You pick up.
note: Rising tone — the universal phone-answer reflex.

text: You catch yourself mid-yawn in a dead-quiet room.
You lean into your coworker's doorway; they look up.
note: The natural way to ask for a quick moment.

text: Two people are deep in conversation and you need to jump in.
note: Softens the interruption before you speak.

text: A tray smashes somewhere behind you; the whole café flinches.
note: Sympathetic wince at someone else's little disaster.

text: Your friend texts: 'I'm so sorry, I can't make it tonight.'
note: Offers a friendly reschedule instead of guilt.

text: Your friend nails the presentation and walks off stage toward you.
note: High-energy congrats. 'You killed it!' is the twin.

text: Someone slides a wrapped gift across the table to you.
Your friend bursts in, glowing: 'Guess what — we're engaged!'
note: Let the surprise land before the congrats.

text: The host swings the door open the moment you arrive.
note: The go-to line walking into someone's home.

text: Your friend pulls someone over: 'This is Alex, finally!'
sample: Ah, I've heard so much about you!

text: As you head out the door, your friend calls: 'Text me when you're home safe!'
Your friend holds up two shirts: 'Okay — which one?'
sample: Ooh, I'd go with the blue one.
note: Natural way to give a confident pick.

text: You blank completely and call someone by the wrong name.
note: Light way to laugh off forgetting a name.

text: Standup. The room turns to you for your update.
note: Signals a short, tidy update's coming.

text: Your boss praises your work in front of the whole team.
note: Graceful deflection that shares the credit.

text: You need to duck out of the meeting early; you unmute.
sample: I've gotta jump to another call—
note: The standard polite exit on calls.

text: The client nods at your demo: 'This looks great.'
A coworker drops into the chair beside you: 'What a day.'
It's the new hire's first morning and they look a little lost.
A ping pops up: 'Could you take a look at this when you get a sec?'
Your manager: 'Any chance you can stay late tonight?' You can't.
sample: Ah, I wish I could, but I've gotta run.

text: Someone leans in: 'Okay, honest opinion — what do you think?'
note: 'Honestly' buys a beat and sounds sincere.

text: The group's stuck picking a restaurant, and everyone looks at you.
note: Easygoing reflex to break the deadlock.

text: A friend pitches a spur-of-the-moment road trip this weekend.
'So, how was the movie?' they ask. It was pretty mediocre.
note: Lukewarm verdict — the 'eh' says it all.

text: A glass tips off the counter and you snatch it out of the air.
note: Relief reflex after a lucky grab.

text: A barista calls your name and slides the cup across.
note: Warm, natural thanks with a little extra.

text: The cashier counts out your change.
note: The tipping reflex at a counter or cab.

text: Someone waves you ahead of them in a long line.
Your card gets declined at checkout.
sample: Oh — weird, let me try another.
note: Stay calm and pivot without fuss.

text: A stranger points down: 'Hey, your shoe's untied.'
sample: Oh — thanks for the heads up!

text: The delivery driver holds out your package.
You sneeze and the person beside you says 'Bless you.'
A stranger admires your dog on your walk.
note: Friendly reflex when your pet gets attention.

text: You grab a cart someone was already using.
note: Quick check before you take something.

text: The bus starts pulling away as you jog up.
You knock your glass and water spreads across the table.
sample: Oops — let me wipe that up.
note: Own the small mess and fix it.

text: A telemarketer calls right in the middle of dinner.
A stranger tips their umbrella over you in the downpour.
sample: Oh, you're a saint — thank you!
note: Warm thanks for an unexpected kindness.

text: You both reach for the last one on the shelf.
sample: Oh — go ahead, you take it.
note: Graceful way to let them have it.

text: The waiter leans in: 'Save room for dessert?'
sample: I'm so tempted, but I'm good.
note: Charming way to decline a treat.

text: Your phone blares in a silent waiting room.
sample: Ugh, sorry — let me grab that.

text: The barista hands you the wrong drink.
sample: Oh, no worries — could I swap it?
note: Polite fix for a mixed-up order.

text: You step toward a packed elevator.
A little kid on the train waves at you.
note: Warm, playful greeting to a child.

text: You nudge the table and their coffee sloshes.
sample: Oh gosh — did I get you?

text: Someone stands to offer you their seat.
sample: Oh, that's okay — you go ahead.

text: The cashier calls after you: 'Have a good one!'
Your neighbor waves from across the yard.
You look up and realize you're at the wrong platform.
A stranger holds the door and waits for you.
Your friend flips their phone around to show baby photos.
note: Gush over the specifics, not just 'cute.'

text: You raise your glasses, just the two of you.
Your friend blurts: 'I finally quit my job!'
You walk in and everyone leaps out: 'SURPRISE!'
Your friend stumbles but stays upright.
Your friend, sheepish: 'I think I messed up big time.'
You finally call back after going quiet for days.
Your friend gives a toast that's all about you.
sample: Aw, stop — you're gonna make me cry.

text: Your friend flies out for a month tomorrow.
sample: Safe travels — text me when you land!

text: You bump into a teacher from years ago.
sample: Oh wow — Mr. Lee! It's really you.

text: Your friend beams: 'We're having a baby!'
Someone unwraps the present you picked out.
sample: Oh good — I hoped you'd like it!
note: Warm reflex as they open your gift.

text: Your friend's team just lost the final.
Your friend asks to crash on your couch tonight.
sample: Yeah, of course — my place is yours.

text: You accidentally start talking at the same time.
Your friend hasn't heard the big news yet.
note: The reflex before you spill it.

text: Your friend drives across town to pick you up.
Your friend goes quiet, eyes welling up.
The toast goes up: 'To the happy couple!'
note: Echo the toast back with the room.

text: Your friend, jittery before a date: 'Do I look okay?'
note: Hype them up on the way out.

text: You run into a coworker at the grocery store.
note: The reflex for an out-of-context run-in.

text: Your friend's nervous for you to meet their parents.
sample: Don't worry — I'll be on my best behavior.

text: Good news lands and a group hug starts forming.
Your friend nails a hard audition and finds you after.
sample: Are you kidding? You were incredible!

text: A friend apologizes for venting too long.
sample: Stop it — that's what I'm here for.

text: Interviewer: 'So — any questions for us?'
You dial in: 'Can everyone hear me okay?'
You start presenting but nothing's on screen.
sample: Can you all see my screen?

text: Your boss: 'Really great work this quarter.'
sample: Thank you — that means a lot.

text: A coworker pings: 'Got time for a quick call?'
You accidentally talk over someone on the call.
The meeting spirals into the weeds.
note: Corporate reflex to park a tangent.

text: The new intern apologizes for a basic question.
sample: Great question — no dumb questions here.

text: An upset client vents down the phone.
sample: I totally understand — let's fix this.

text: You're asked something you can't answer yet.
sample: Good question — let me get back to you.

text: The deadline just jumped up a week.
A teammate thanks you for unblocking them.
You have to gently correct your manager.
sample: Hmm — actually, I think it's the other way.

text: Standup reaches you and there's nothing new.
sample: Nothing new from me — carrying on.

text: The call's wrapping up.
You get CC'd on an urgent fire drill.
sample: On it — taking a look now.

text: A coworker announces they're leaving the company.
sample: We're gonna miss you around here.

text: You realize you mangled the client's name.
sample: Sorry — did I say that right?

text: Your boss asks where the project stands.
sample: Almost there — just polishing it up.

text: The presentation clicker dies mid-slide.
sample: Bear with me — tech's fighting me.

text: A coworker offers to grab you a coffee.
You push the final commit on a big project.
An email lands praising your work out of nowhere.
sample: Oh, wow — that made my day.

text: Someone asks if you can mentor the new hire.
'Coffee or tea?' — you honestly don't care.
Your friend: 'Isn't this place amazing?'
Someone floats a risky plan and waits.
'Should we just go for it?' they ask.
sample: You know what? Let's do it.

text: 'Be honest — is this too much?'
A friend raves about a show you couldn't stand.
sample: Really? It just wasn't for me.

text: 'What do you think of the new design?' — you love it.
The plan sounds shaky but you stay polite.
'Am I overreacting?' your friend asks.
You're asked to pick between two options.
sample: Tough call — I'd lean toward the first.

text: Someone drops a wild opinion at dinner.
note: Playful reaction to a bold claim.

text: Your friend defends something ridiculous.
'Was that meeting useful?' — it wasn't.
Someone makes a genuinely strong point.
'Do you like it?' — you love it.
You're put on the spot but truly unsure.
sample: Honestly, I could go either way.

text: Your friend suggests skipping the gym.
Someone's idea turns out to be brilliant.
'Spicy or mild?' — you live for spice.
'Is this outfit too loud?' your friend asks.
sample: Nah — you can pull it off.

text: The debate heats up and you give ground.
'Is my plan crazy?' they ask.
sample: A little — but I'm into it.

text: 'Think it'll actually work?' — you doubt it.
sample: Eh — I wouldn't bet on it.

text: 'Too early to leave the party?'
Someone asks for your gut feeling.
'Was it worth the money?' — not really.
The lights flicker, then everything goes dark.
You freeze at your desk — did you leave the stove on?
